newsitem.title: USA: Bristol-Myers's drug and consumer product sales up.
newsitem.headline: Bristol-Myers's drug and consumer product sales up.

text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co said Tuesday it first quarter sales increased 10 percent, driven by strength in pharmaceutical and consumer products.

Although sales were dampened by unfavorable foreign exchange rate fluctuations, total sales increased to $4.0 billion from $3.7 billion a year earlier. Domestic sales increased 11 percent, while international sales rose nine percent, the company said.
Pharmaceutical product sales increased 12 percent. Excluding CAPOTEN, sales of pharmaceutical products increased 20 percent, the company said.
Consumer product sales increased 10 percent, primarily as a result of strong volume growth in the company's hair care product lines which grew 25 percent over the prior year.

Nutritional product sales grew 12 percent, led by Enfamil, the company's largest selling infant formula, as well as Prosobee, Nutramigen and Lactofree special infant formulas, in both U.S. and international markets.
Medical device product sales dropped one percent. This unit would have seen an increase of two percent if the unfavorable effect of foreign exchange were excluded.
